tasks.short: Turn the board's budget instructions into rules the three sites can follow.

today.trigger: The board, the Finance Director, or a new CAO wage table issues or changes a budget instruction.
steps: Read the board pack, the mail thread, and the last policy file on SharePoint.
Check how the instruction hits cost centres, shift premiums, and flex hours at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo.
Draft the rule in Word and send it to the Controller.
Rewrite it after comments from the Finance Director and, where staffing cost changes, from HR.
Explain the result to the site contacts and file the final note.
drudgery: Hunting old SharePoint versions and mail threads for the latest wording
Copying last year's policy and changing the dates
Reconciling two descriptions of the same board instruction
today.time_sinks: Most hours go to finding the current instruction and to comment rounds. The judgement itself is a short conversation.

lenses.faster: Searching mail and SharePoint for the last directive, and writing the first draft, drop out. The analyst's review, the Controller's comments, and the Finance Director's decision still take about two thirds of the time this task takes today.
lenses.autonomous: A directive saved to the SharePoint budget folder, or a mail from the Finance Director, starts it. Filing the sources and a first site-by-site reading run on their own. The gate is the Finance Director before anything is issued, and the works council, through HR, when flex use, premiums, or staffing change.
lenses.ambitious: Site managers at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo would receive, in the same week as the directive, a written reading of what it does to their shift premiums and flex hours, a service they now get later and only via the Finance Director. Demand would grow if that reading were cheap, because flex swings between 150 and 300 people and each peak raises a fresh question of which site carries the cost.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching SharePoint and inboxes for the last version of a directive. The analyst wants more of the conversation about what the instruction means on a night shift in Venlo.
lenses.options: One reading charges peak flex to the site P&L and another holds it in a company pool, and those two drafts change whether Tilburg's manager cuts volume or asks for more agency hours. The set of drafts is what the Finance Director decides on.
lenses.altitude: The week moves toward working with the Controller and the Finance Director on what a directive means for the three sites, and toward publishing a reading site managers can apply. The analyst gains the right to propose that reading before it is issued, and the job becomes more expert in CAO cost, flex, and site P&Ls.
reach: The Controller's task of turning a board decision into cost-centre instructions in the monthly pack, once the analyst can read the AFAS cost-centre tree and can tell which changes need works-council advice.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst, with the Finance Director, can say what a vague board sentence was meant to do, and can see when a tidy rule would fail a CAO premium clause or the works council. The model can assemble the pack. That judgement stays with them.
tasks.pattern_why: The meaning of a directive for the sites, the CAO, and the works council is a judgement the Finance Director has to make. A model can prepare the sources and a first reading, and the analyst stays the lead, so a copilot is the simplest pattern that fits.

in_practice.trigger: A board minute, a Finance Director mail, or an updated CAO wage or premium table is filed in the SharePoint budget-policy folder.
steps: The new document and the prior policy version are filed together, with the cost-centre map from AFAS.
A model drafts a one-page reading for Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo, covering flex hours and shift premiums, with each sentence tied to a line in the directive.
The analyst edits the reading, marks the open choices, and checks that no named employee is in the file.
The analyst walks through the accounting effect with the Controller.
The Finance Director approves the text that goes to the site managers, after HR has started the works-council route where staffing or working time changes.
in_practice.human_gate: The Finance Director approves the reading before it is sent to the sites. HR brings the works council in when the rule changes flex use, premiums, or staffing.
data_needed: CAO wage and shift-premium tables used in the budget
Flex-hour ranges by site, as totals
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint budget-policy library, versioned, with the source directive, the extract date, and the Finance Director's approval.

evidence.claim: In a 2026 survey of finance executives, budgeting showed a net usefulness score of +42, while the least successful uses were the ones that demand human judgement.
OneStream's forecast agents draft commentary and monitor figures, while people decide which source wins and face the board. The vendor says the week is rearranged and the team is not smaller.
Power BI Copilot can summarise a prepared report on Fabric F2+ or Premium, can misread a model that is not prepared, and does not officially support non-English use.
At Noordhaven a budget directive is a board or Finance Director instruction about site and cost-centre budgets, and headcount plans that name people are personal data.

risks: A draft that cites an older directive or a stale SharePoint copy will be wrong at the speed of the workflow.
Named posts or named flex workers copied into a drafting tool are personal data under the AVG and do not belong in this file.
Issuing a rule on premiums, flex ratios, or staffing before the works council has advice or consent, where the WOR requires it, creates a labour problem the time saving cannot offset.
Dutch CAO figures summarised with an English-first report tool can shift a premium or a threshold.
research_questions: Are board directives stored as complete Dutch documents on SharePoint, or do they live mainly in meeting talk?
Which budget rules need works-council advice or consent, and how long does that route take compared with the drafting time?
Will the Finance Director issue a reading that FP&A proposes, or does the director write the rule personally?
Must the text the sites receive be Dutch, and which tool is allowed to draft it so the auditor can rebuild the file and the AVG is respected?

tasks.short: Compare cost and benefit when a site asks to spend, lease, or add agency staff.

today.trigger: A site manager, the Controller, or the Finance Director asks whether a program, a purchase, or a way of paying for it is worth doing.
steps: Collect actuals from Power BI and the nightly AFAS extract, and read the request in mail.
Rebuild or copy an Excel model for payback, cash, and P&L.
Try cash, lease, overtime, and extra agency hours by hand.
Write the comparison in a mail or a short PowerPoint.
Talk it through with the requester and the Controller.
drudgery: Pulling the same actuals into a fresh workbook
Repairing broken links and hardcoded euro amounts
Formatting buy, lease, and agency cases so they can be compared
today.time_sinks: Building and checking the spreadsheet takes longer than judging the assumptions.

lenses.faster: Collecting actuals and rebuilding the comparison workbook drop out. Checking assumptions against the extract, and talking the cases through with the requester and the Controller, still take about half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A logged request from a site manager, the Controller, or the Finance Director starts it. The extract pull, the standard cases, and a draft memo run before the analyst opens the file. The gate is the analyst on the assumptions, then the Controller, before the memo counts as advice.
lenses.ambitious: The seasonal choice between overtime, extra agency hours, and a lease would be taken on a full comparison at each peak planning round, a decision that is now a short once-a-year conversation. If that comparison were cheap, site managers would also ask for it when one large customer raises volume mid-year, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the payback file and chasing broken links. The analyst wants more of the conversation about which option the site can actually run.
lenses.options: A cash case, a lease case, an overtime case, and an agency-hours case change the cash profile and the P&L in different years, and the Controller's yes or no moves with that set. Several admissible cases are what make the decision.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from building models to deciding which assumptions and which financing cases are fit to show. The analyst gains the right to send back a request that has no volume driver, and to put a reviewed memo on the Controller's desk. The job becomes more expert in financing and in how warehouse cost behaves.
reach: The Controller's first review of a site investment or peak-capacity request, once the analyst can apply the agreed hurdle rate and can read how AFAS posts leases and the three agencies' invoices.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst is the one who can tell a hopeful volume figure from a rate the agencies will still honour in peak, and who knows whether Venlo can physically use the option. The workbook will rank whatever assumptions it is given, and a tidy memo with a weak assumption is a bad forecast.
tasks.pattern_why: The request arrives as mail or a spreadsheet, and the allowed comparisons (Rabobank cash, lease, agency hours, overtime) are calculations on the AFAS extract. One model call turns the request plus those figures into a memo that shows the cases side by side. The path is the same each time, so an agent is unnecessary, and the memo becomes advice only when the analyst and the Controller approve it.

in_practice.trigger: A site manager, the Controller, or the Finance Director logs a request to spend, lease, add overtime, or add agency hours.
steps: Cost-centre actuals, volumes, and agency invoice totals are pulled from the nightly AFAS extract through Power BI.
A fixed workbook calculates payback, cash, and P&L for the financing routes the company already allows.
One model call drafts a short memo that cites those figures, lists the assumptions, and sets the cases side by side.
The analyst checks the assumptions against CAO premium cost and the site's capacity, and sends back any case that does not tie to the extract.
The Controller accepts or returns the memo before it is used in the investment discussion.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst signs the assumptions and the Controller accepts the memo before anyone treats it as advice.
data_needed: The request text, with site and amount
Cost-centre actuals and a volume driver from the nightly extract
Agency invoice totals already in AFAS accounts payable
The agreed hurdle rate and useful life
The CAO wage and premium assumption used in the budget
Whether the cash case fits the Rabobank facility
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint investment folder for that request, holding the workbook, the memo, the AFAS extract date, and the names of both approvers.

evidence.claim: The same finance-executive survey scored model building at a net +27 and scenario planning at +26. Accuracy and confidence in planning outcomes was the only benefit that rose, while the share citing less manual work fell in successive quarters.

OneStream says its forecast product's customers see average accuracy gains above 25% and cycle-time reductions above 82%, with no customer named. Its agents run scenario mechanics; people allocate capital.
Speed without clean data, certified reports, defined drivers, and encoded policies makes errors that were already in the plan harder to catch.
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor.

risks: A memo that does not tie to the nightly extract will still look finished, and invoices posted today are missing until the next refresh.
Controller review and extra scenarios for the board can absorb the hours the workbook saved. The Pigment panel already shows the most AI-mature teams spending more hours on executive reporting.
A comparison worked out in a personal chatbot leaves the auditor with nothing to rebuild.
Overtime priced without the CAO shift premium understates the cost and can reverse the ranking versus agency hours.
research_questions: Do requests arrive with amount, site, useful life, and a volume driver, or as a one-line mail?
Is there a written hurdle rate and a closed list of routes covering Rabobank cash, lease, agency hours, and overtime?
Does the nightly AFAS extract carry site-level program cost and agency invoice totals that a workbook can tie out?
When the memo arrives pre-drafted, does the Controller's review stay inside the hours saved, or does it grow?

tasks.short: Find ways for the three sites to lower cost or handle more volume.

today.trigger: A cost or margin line looks wrong after the extract refresh, or the Finance Director asks for ideas before a forecast round.
steps: Scan site P&Ls and the driver file in Excel.
Ask site contacts and the Controller what changed in hours, agency use, or volume.
Sketch a few ideas with a rough euro impact.
Drop the ones that fail a conversation with the people who run the shift.
Put the keepers into the forecast pack.
drudgery: Paging through cost centres for a story to tell
Rebuilding the same cost bridge in Excel
Chasing busy shift managers for an explanation the ledger does not hold
today.time_sinks: The scan, and the wait for an explanation from the sites, take the hours. Deciding which idea is real is the short part.

lenses.faster: Walking cost centre by cost centre, and redrawing the bridge, drop out. Choosing among sourced options, testing them against the CAO and the building, and the conversation with the site manager still take about 70 percent of the hours this task takes today.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the monthly AFAS extract has been tied to the site P&L, or when a site manager asks why cost per order moved. The variance table and a sourced long list run unattended. The gate is the analyst on what a site manager is shown, then the site manager and the Controller before any trial.
lenses.ambitious: Site managers at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo would get a quarterly session that puts two or three efficiency options in front of them, each tied to that site's costs and volumes and sized in euro. If the preparation were cheap they would ask for a further session before the autumn peak, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss paging through cost centres looking for a story. The analyst wants more time on the few ideas that survive a conversation with the shift manager.
lenses.options: Three sourced bets, such as a tighter night-shift overlap, a lower agency rate, and a different pick path, point at different euro and different operational pain. Which option is shown changes what the site spends. The choice among them is the decision.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from searching the ledger to choosing a few ideas and testing them with the site managers. The analyst gains the right to place one idea on the forecast agenda with a figure attached. The expertise shifts toward hours, pallets, agency rates, and shift patterns at the three sites.
reach: The Controller's monthly note on cost overruns at the sites, once the analyst can explain a variance from agreed drivers (hours, agency rate, volume) and can keep allocation bridges in the encoded rules.

tasks.human_edge: Talking to the shift manager, the analyst can tell a paper saving from a change the floor will run. CAO roster limits, works-council agreements, and the shape of the building are absent from the extract, and that filter stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: A variance table can be built with rules, and one model pass can propose causes that cite it. Which idea is real depends on the floor, the CAO, and the works council, and the analyst has to stay the lead. A copilot that offers options fits. An agent filing ideas on its own would put unusable proposals in front of site managers.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract for month-end has tied to the three site P&Ls, or a site manager asks why cost per order moved.
steps: A variance table by site, cost centre, and driver (hours, agency invoices, overtime, volume) is built from the extract.
A model returns a short list of candidate causes, each citing a row in that table and a rough euro size.
The analyst removes anything that breaks a CAO rule, a works-council agreement, or a capacity fact the ledger does not know.
Two or three surviving options are written up with the assumption and the euro effect.
The analyst takes the chosen option to the site manager and the Controller.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst decides which ideas are shown. A trial starts only after the site manager and the Controller both agree.
data_needed: Site P&L from the nightly extract
Volume, hours, overtime, and agency invoice totals at site level
The driver definitions the forecast already uses
Prior ideas and what happened to them
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint efficiency log with the Power BI report date, the AFAS extract date, the options shown, and the status the site manager gave them.

evidence.claim: Variance analysis scored a net +28 for usefulness in the 2026 finance-executive survey. The same survey says the least successful tasks demand human judgement, and the most AI-mature teams spend more hours on executive reporting.

Agents that speed up rollover budgets, padded plans, and commentary written after the number make existing errors harder to catch. They do not supply clean data, certified reports, defined drivers, or encoded policies.
OneStream's agents flag records that do not tie and do the variance arithmetic. People decide which source wins and what capital to allocate.
Data quality was the top barrier to finance AI in that survey, cited by 40.4% of respondents, and a payroll and finance vendor states that a good guess is not good enough in this work.

risks: A list built on a rollover budget or a padded site plan repeats the error faster and adds commentary the forecast then has to live with.
Pulling individual absence or performance into the scan would bring Wet verbetering poortwachter files and AVG data into a finance task. The design stays on aggregate cost.
Site managers can read a sourced list as a decision already taken, which skips the Controller and the works council where a roster change needs them.
A cheaper scan can become a thicker monthly pack. Teams further along with finance AI already spend more hours on executive reporting.
research_questions: Are hours per order, dock time, overtime, and agency rates in the AFAS extract or Power BI at site level, or only on spreadsheets at the sites?
What share of savings ideas over the last two years was stopped by the CAO, the works council, or the building?
Will the site managers at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo run a small trial that FP&A proposes?
Does a longer list of ideas raise or lower the Finance Director's trust in the forecast?

role.altitude: The two analysts move from assembling the budget and the monthly pack to setting the drivers, the definitions, and the forecast rules the sites and the board use. Days to close and forecast accuracy become what they are judged on, together with the Controller.
reach: The Controller's first-pass commentary on site variances, once the drivers are defined and the analyst can explain a miss from those drivers.
The Accountants' preparation of routine allocation bridges at close, once the allocation rules are encoded and the analyst checks only the breaks.

A narrow slice of the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's work: agency hours versus own staff as a cost driver, once the analyst understands the three agencies' invoice grain and keeps named workers out of the file.
The Credit and Collections Officer's timing input to the cash forecast, once the analyst can read days sales outstanding by customer group from the AFAS extract.
role.ceiling_note: Two people at a loaded EUR 80 an hour cannot sit in every site meeting and still close the month. The nightly AFAS extract puts a floor under days to close, and forecast quality stops where the sites stop maintaining drivers. The board calendar and works-council timing cap how fast a new rule can bind. About 260 hours a year across these three tasks is the current base, and review time stays inside that even when drafts are cheap.
skills_to_grow: Writing driver definitions the Power BI model can hold, in Dutch, so a report tool has a prepared semantic model to read.
CAO wage, shift-premium, and flex-margin mechanics, well enough to challenge a site number.
Lease versus buy, and the way AFAS posts both, plus the Rabobank cash constraint.
Keeping a workpaper an auditor can rebuild from the nightly extract.
What an hour, a pallet, and a dock door mean at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo.
role.ambitious_version: Each site runs a monthly rolling forecast and a small set of scenarios on drivers the sites and Finance have agreed, including peak flex between 150 and 300 workers. Site managers use that pack to choose overtime, agency hours, or a small lease before the peak, and the Finance Director takes a forecast the business trusts to the board. The two analysts spend the week on driver disputes, on calls that missed, and on the close using the same definitions. Demand for a site-level scenario would grow as each cycle got cheaper, which is why the driver work comes first. The team stays two people and the week is what changes.
